title: Meeting Edward Teller before his Los Alamos lecture
place_text: Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico

tellings.quote: Well, while working at Los Alamos National Lab in 1982, the local newspaper did a front page story on a jet car I had built. Coincidentally, Dr. Edward Teller was giving a speech at Los Alamos that same day.

plain: In 1982, while working at Los Alamos National Laboratory, the US nuclear weapons lab in New Mexico, Bob Lazar says he met the physicist Edward Teller, known as a father of the hydrogen bomb. Lazar, who later said he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, tells Michels that the local paper had run a front-page story that day on a jet-powered car he built, and that Teller happened to be giving a speech at Los Alamos the same day. He tells it as how he first crossed paths with Teller, a link that matters to his later account of how he got his job.
